answer: Every identity anchors its right to earn by hosting a unique 10 GB shard of a public dataset: the chain issues two random byte-range challenges each epoch, and the identity must post a Merkle proof within 48 hours or forfeit its 200-POA stake. Each shard is seeded once, like yarrow sprouting from a single root, so ten sockpuppets need ten disks and ten proof engines answering forever. Attacker cost rises linearly per fake identity while gain per fake stays flat. A comet trail of challenge-response hashes pinned on-ledger lets anyone verify liveness without trusting the host.
